source: own minimal TCP (fps-tcp) on sandbox own newreno
notes: the client side and the server side are two instances of the own TCP state machine in one process, joined by an in memory pair of frame queues of fps-backend-afxdp, so there is no kernel socket and no descriptor

frames are Ethernet (802.1Q tagged when --own-vlan is set) with IPv4 and TCP, with an IP header checksum and a TCP checksum that are computed on send and verified on receive; the MAC address of host i of a pool is mac_base + i and the neighbor of an address is read from the HST-03 table of fps-hosts

the client side is a pool of hosts (--own-pool) and the server side a pool of hosts (--own-server-hosts); the connection table is keyed by the 4-tuple of both addresses and both ports, and a connect takes the next client host in turn

loss recovery (TRN-23): a round trip estimator with the retransmission timeout of RFC 6298 (minimum 200 ms, Karn's rule, exponential backoff), fast retransmit on three duplicate acknowledgments with Limited Transmit, an out of order receive queue, and NewReno with an initial window of 10 segments; the state sits in a box that a connection holds only while data is in flight or waits behind a hole

options for long fat paths (TRN-24): window scaling (RFC 7323, a 1 MiB receive buffer gives a shift of 5), timestamps (round trip samples and PAWS), selective acknowledgment (RFC 2018 blocks from the out of order queue and the scoreboard and pipe of RFC 6675 beside NewReno), and a delayed acknowledgment (every second segment or 40 ms, at once for out of order data); each is offered in the SYN and used when the peer offers it too; the scoreboard lives in the box of the connection, so an idle socket holds only 6 bytes of option state

congestion control (TRN-25): CUBIC (RFC 9438: the cubic window function of the time since the last event, a decrease to 0.7, fast convergence, and the reno friendly region; ported from smoltcp 0.14.0) is the default and NewReno stays selectable (--own-cc); the CUBIC state is part of the box of the connection, so an idle socket pays nothing for it
timers live in a heap with one entry per connection, so a poll with idle sockets does not grow with the socket count, where a stack that walks its sockets does
a closed tuple is held for one second in TIME-WAIT instead of minutes, so a rate run does not run out of ports
bytes_per_socket is the growth of the resident set of the process and includes the connection table, the buffers that the held sockets own (none while idle), and the frame link

the link is the impaired link of TRN-22 (loss 0%, delay 20 ms, reorder 0%, rate 1000 Mbit/s with a queue of 4096 KiB per direction), which wraps the frame queues of the stack; retransmissions are counted at the link as data segments that start below the highest sequence number sent before
sockets counts both hosts of a pair and includes the listening sockets

loss workload: one session sends 4194304 bytes and the transfer is complete when the server has confirmed the count; goodput is the confirmed bytes over the time from the first write to that confirmation, and counts as 0 for a transfer that did not complete; the link is loss 0%, delay 20 ms, reorder 0%, rate 1000 Mbit/s with a queue of 4096 KiB per direction, with the loss shown per row
a metric of the loss workload is the mean over its transfers, and the key has the loss in percent with p for the decimal point

fairness run (TRN-25): every flow sends without end, the goodput is the sum of the bytes that the server received from all flows in the measurement window over the window (the warm-up before it is not counted), and jain_index is (sum x)^2 / (n sum x^2) over the bytes of the flows; retransmits count the whole run, the warm-up included
